Two-stage sequential photoredox flow design. Stage 1 (FEP 10 mL coil, 1 mm ID, Kessil A160WE 450 nm): Ir(III)*-mediated SET oxidation of PMPSCH2TMS generates α-thiomethyl radical I; Giese addition onto acrylonitrile gives sulfide 3a. Strictly O2-free — offline argon sparging replaces forbidden inline degasser. Stage 2 (PFA 20 mL coil, 1.5 mm ID, Penn PhD M2 450 nm): air introduced via T2 creates gas-liquid segmented (Taylor) flow; Ir(III)* mediates aerobic sulfoxidation via SET/superoxide and EnT/singlet O2 pathways. Analogy 1 (Ir photoredox radical addition, 30 min RT, 2 mm quartz, 48× speedup) confirms ~30 min residence time feasibility for Stage 1. Analogy 3 (Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6, FEP tubing, 12 min, segmented flow) directly validates FEP tubing and segmented flow approach for this catalyst class. Da = 1.75 (transition zone) — static mixer insert at T1 recommended if yield is suboptimal.

# Flow Chemistry Design Brief: Two-Stage Photoredox Giese Addition / Aerobic Sulfoxidation

---

## (1) Proposed Flow Setup

**Reaction:** One-pot photoredox Giese radical C–C bond formation (Stage 1) followed by aerobic sulfoxidation (Stage 2), converting PMPSCH₂TMS (1a) + acrylonitrile (2a) → sulfide 3a → sulfoxide 4a, catalyzed by Ir(dF(CF₃)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ (0.5 mol%) at 450 nm.

### Hardware Configuration

**Three feed streams → two sequential irradiated coil reactors → BPR → collection**

| Stream | Contents | Concentration | Flow Rate | Pump |
|--------|----------|---------------|-----------|------|
| A | PMPSCH₂TMS (1a, 0.2 M) + Ir catalyst (0.001 M) in pre-degassed EtOH/pH 9 buffer (5:1 v/v) | 0.2 M substrate | 0.197 mL/min | HPLC pump |
| B | Acrylonitrile (2a, 0.4 M) in pre-degassed EtOH/pH 9 buffer (5:1 v/v) | 0.4 M | 0.197 mL/min | Syringe pump |
| C | Air (21% O₂) | gas phase | 4.2005 sccm (MFC) | MFC or gas-tight syringe |

**Post-mixing concentrations:** [1a] = 0.1 M, [2a] = 0.2 M (2.0 equiv), [Ir] = 0.5 mol% relative to 1a.

**Total liquid flow rate: 0.39357 mL/min**

### Stage 1 — Giese Radical Addition (O₂-free)

- **Reactor:** FEP coil, 1.0 mm ID
- **Volume:** 38.1305 mL total system (see note below on screen)
- **Residence time:** 8.3 min (inlet/STP basis)
- **Temperature:** 25.0 °C
- **Light:** Kessil A160WE, 450.0 nm, 40 W — coil wrapped around or adjacent to lamp
- **Atmosphere:** Strictly argon (no inline degasser; offline sparging protocol, see §3)
- **Mixing:** T-junction T1 combines streams A + B before reactor inlet

### Stage 2 — Aerobic Sulfoxidation (gas–liquid segmented flow)

- **Reactor:** PFA coil, 1.5 mm ID
- **Light:** Penn PhD M2, 450.0 nm, 30 W
- **Temperature:** 25.0 °C
- **Gas introduction:** T-junction T2 at Stage 1 outlet; air (stream C) enters here to create Taylor (slug) flow
- **Gas flow:** 4.2005 sccm air via MFC → actual volumetric flow 0.7726 mL/min at reactor conditions
- **Gas holdup:** 0.6625 (66% of channel volume is gas phase)
- **BPR:** 3.0 bar installed at system outlet

### Plumbing Sequence

```
[Pump A] ──┐
           T1 ──→ [Stage 1 FEP coil, 450 nm, 40 W, argon atmosphere]
[Pump B] ──┘                                    │
                                                 ▼
                              T2 ←── [Air MFC, 4.2005 sccm]
                                                 │
                                                 ▼
                              [Stage 2 PFA coil, 450 nm, 30 W, air/liquid slug flow]
                                                 │
                                                 ▼
                                          [BPR, 3.0 bar]
                                                 │
                                                 ▼
                                          [Product collection]
```

**Critical constraint:** T2 must be placed strictly downstream of the Stage 1 reactor outlet. Air must never contact Stage 1.

---

## (2) Why These Conditions Were Chosen

### Wavelength: 450 nm
Ir(dF(CF₃)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ has its MLCT absorption band centered at ~380–450 nm. The batch protocol uses 452 nm. Both the Kessil A160WE and Penn PhD M2 emit at 450 nm — direct match. This catalyst class was validated in flow at 440–450 nm in segmented-flow FEP systems (DOI: **10.1039/D1RE00271F**).

### FEP/PFA tubing and coil geometry
FEP (Stage 1) and PFA (Stage 2) are UV/visible-transparent, chemically inert to EtOH/aqueous buffer, and rated well above operating pressure. The 1.0 mm ID in Stage 1 gives an optical path ≤1 mm versus ~10–15 mm in a typical batch flask — this is the primary photon-delivery intensification mechanism. The 1.5 mm ID in Stage 2 accommodates gas–liquid slug flow without excessive pressure drop. FEP tubing with this exact catalyst class [Ir(dF(CF₃)ppy)₂(dtbbpy)PF₆] in segmented flow is directly precedented (DOI: **10.1039/D1RE00271F**, 12 min residence time, segmented flow).

### Two-stage sequential design
Stage 1 must be O₂-free: the α-thiomethyl radical intermediate I is quenched by O₂, which would terminate the radical chain before Giese addition occurs. mechanism_steps.description: Photoexcitation of Ir(III) ground state to Ir(III)* excited state by 450 nm blue light absorption
SET oxidation of PMPSCH2TMS (1a) by Ir(III)* to generate cation radical 1a•+ and Ir(II)
Desilylation of cation radical 1a•+ (loss of TMS+) to generate α-thiomethyl radical I
Giese radical addition of α-thiomethyl radical I onto acrylonitrile (2a) to form adduct radical II
SET reduction of radical adduct II by Ir(II) to form carbanion III, regenerating Ir(III) ground state (turnover)
Protonation of carbanion III by EtOH/buffer solvent to give sulfide product 3a
Stage 2 — SET pathway: Ir(III)* oxidizes sulfide 3a to sulfide radical cation; Ir(II) reduces O2 to superoxide O2•−; superoxide oxidizes sulfide radical cation to sulfoxide 4a
Stage 2 — EnT pathway: Ir(III)* sensitizes triplet O2 (³O₂) to singlet oxygen (¹O₂) via Dexter energy transfer; ¹O₂ oxidizes sulfide 3a to sulfoxide 4a

Photocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF₃)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ Loading: 0.5 mol% Excited state redox: Ir(III)/Ir(II) = +1.21 V vs. SCE Ground state reductive: Ir(III)/Ir(II) = −1.37 V vs. SCE Solvent: EtOH / pH 9 aqueous buffer (5:1 v/v) Concentration: 0.1 M Oxidant: Molecular oxygen (O₂) from air — introduced only in Step 2 PROCEDURE (TWO SEQUENTIAL STEPS, ONE POT) STEP 1 — C–C Bond Formation (Giese Radical Addition): Atmosphere: Argon (strictly O₂-free) Light source: 10 W blue LED, 452 nm Temperature: 25°C (room temperature) Reaction time: 4 hours Vessel: Sealed pressure tube Outcome: Sulfide 3a formed, 92% yield Mechanism: Ir(III) oxidizes 1a via SET → cationic radical 1a•+ → desilylation → α-thiomethyl radical I → Giese addition onto acrylonitrile 2a → radical II → reduced by Ir(II) → carbanion III → protonated by solvent → sulfide 3a STEP 2 — Aerobic Oxidation (Sulfide → Sulfoxide): Atmosphere: Air (O₂ introduced after Step 1 complete) Light source: 10 W blue LED, 452 nm (same source, kept on) Temperature: 25°C Reaction time: 6 hours Vessel: Same tube, opened to air Outcome: Sulfoxide 4a formed, 95% yield Mechanism: Two parallel pathways — (a) SET: Ir(III)* oxidizes sulfide 3a + O₂ → superoxide → sulfoxide (b) EnT: Ir(III)* converts ³O₂ → ¹O₂ (singlet oxygen) → sulfoxide Sulfide oxidation potential: Eox(3a) = +1.13 V vs. SCE SENSITIVITY FLAGS O₂ during Step 1: CRITICAL — O₂ quenches α-thiomethyl radical I → reaction fails completely Light: ESSENTIAL — no conversion without LED Photocatalyst: ESSENTIAL — no conversion without [Ir] pH control: IMPORTANT — pH 9 buffer suppresses byproduct PMPSCH₃ (1a-I) via protonation of radical intermediate Moisture: TOLERANT — aqueous buffer intentional Scale in batch: PROBLEMATIC — uneven irradiation and poor O₂ mass transfer at >0.2 mmol TOTAL BATCH TIME: 10 hours (4h + 6h) TOTAL BATCH YIELD: 95% isolated (sulfoxide 4a) SCALE: 0.2 mmol

_analogies.summary: This photoredox catalysis process involves a radical addition followed by oxidation using fac-[Ir(ppy)3] as the photocatalyst with 425 nm LED irradiation. The reaction was performed in DMSO solvent at 25°C using a MiChS flow photoreactor L-1 (M) with 2 mm ID quartz tubing and a 2.7 mL reactor volume. The flow process achieved a remarkable 30-minute residence time at 0.09 mL/min flow rate, compared to 24 hours required in batch conditions. Flow chemistry provided dramatic improvements with a 48-fold reduction in reaction time (from 24 hours to 30 minutes) and a substantial increase in yield from 22% in batch to 75% in flow. The enhanced performance in flow resulted from improved light penetration and better mass transfer in the thin quartz tubing, enabling more efficient photocatalytic activation and faster reaction kinetics.

_analogies.summary: This photocatalyzed radical addition employs 2-benzopyrylium intermediates generated in situ as the photoredox catalyst under 450 nm LED irradiation. The flow process operates in a 1.0 mL photochemical reactor using 1,2-dichloroethane as solvent at room temperature (25°C) with a 2.5 minute residence time and 24.0 mL/min flow rate, achieving 77% yield. In contrast, the batch baseline required elevated temperature (50°C) and 60 minutes reaction time to obtain 76% yield. Flow processing provided a 24-fold intensification in reaction rate while maintaining comparable yield and enabling safer room temperature operation, demonstrating superior scalability for this photoredox transformation.

_analogies.summary: This photoredox cross-coupling reaction utilizes single electron transfer (SET) mechanism with Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photocatalyst (2 mol%) and tBu-TMG base in DMF solvent under 440 nm blue LED irradiation. The optimized flow process operates at 50°C with a 12-minute residence time at 0.83 mL/min flow rate in a segmented flow reactor using FEP tubing with 10 mL reactor volume. Flow conditions achieved 88% yield compared to 81% yield under batch conditions at 30°C, representing an 8.6% improvement in yield. The primary advantage of flow was enabling higher operating temperature (50°C vs 30°C) with superior heat transfer control, while providing predictable scale-up capability to hundreds of mg/h production rates with significantly shorter reaction times.

Purge all Stage 1 tubing (from pump heads to Stage 1 reactor outlet) with pre-degassed solvent under argon before starting the reaction to displace any residual O2.
Verify Stage 2 T-junction (T2) is downstream of Stage 1 reactor outlet before opening air feed.

Engineering calculations: BPR required at 5.9 bar; select 5 bar BPR from available inventory [5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 50.0] bar — closest available below calculated value; 10 bar is also acceptable if 5 bar causes instability.

pre_council_proposal.chemistry_notes: Two-stage sequential photoredox flow design. Stage 1 (FEP 10 mL coil, 1 mm ID, Kessil A160WE 450 nm): Ir(III)*-mediated SET oxidation of PMPSCH2TMS generates α-thiomethyl radical I; Giese addition onto acrylonitrile gives sulfide 3a. Strictly O2-free — offline argon sparging replaces forbidden inline degasser. Stage 2 (PFA 20 mL coil, 1.5 mm ID, Penn PhD M2 450 nm): air introduced via T2 creates gas-liquid segmented (Taylor) flow; Ir(III)* mediates aerobic sulfoxidation via SET/superoxide and EnT/singlet O2 pathways. Key design decisions: (1) FEP 1 mm ID for Stage 1 gives ~1 mm optical path vs ~10-15 mm in batch — primary intensification driver; (2) PFA 1.5 mm ID for Stage 2 accommodates gas-liquid slug flow with good kLa; (3) total liquid flow 0.5 mL/min from engineering calculations (τ = 28.6 min target, V_R = 10+20 = 30 mL total); (4) Stage 1 residence time = 10 mL / 0.5 mL/min = 20 min (vs 4 h batch, 12× reduction); Stage 2 residence time = 20 mL / 0.5 mL/min = 40 min (vs 6 h batch, 9× reduction); total = 60 min vs 600 min batch (10× overall); (5) BPR 5 bar required for gas-liquid system; (6) pH 9 buffer co-solvent suppresses PMPSCH3 byproduct. Analogy 1 (Ir photoredox radical addition, 30 min RT, 2 mm quartz, 48× speedup) confirms ~30 min residence time feasibility for Stage 1. Analogy 3 (Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6, FEP tubing, 12 min, segmented flow) directly validates FEP tubing and segmented flow approach for this catalyst class. Da = 1.75 (transition zone) — static mixer insert at T1 recommended if yield is suboptimal.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Engineering calculations: τ = 28.6 min (range 11.1–150 min, IF = 21×). Available reactors: 10 mL FEP (Stage 1) + 20 mL PFA (Stage 2) = 30 mL total at 0.5 mL/min liquid flow → τ_total = 60 min, within the calculated range. Stage 1 τ = 20 min (vs analogy 1: 30 min for similar Ir photoredox radical addition — slightly faster acceptable given 40 W Kessil vs analogy's 0.077 W). Stage 2 τ = 40 min (longer than Stage 1 consistent with batch 6h vs 4h ratio). Analogy 3: 12 min for Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2 FEP segmented flow — our Stage 1 at 20 min is conservative and appropriate given two-stage design.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Stage 1 is single-phase liquid: τ = V_reactor / Q_liquid = 10 mL / 0.5 mL/min = 20 min. Stage 2 is gas-liquid: inlet/STP apparent τ = 20 mL / (0.5 + 5.34) mL/min = 3.4 min; in-channel pressure-corrected τ = 20 mL / (0.5 + 5.83) mL/min = 3.2 min. However, the liquid-phase residence time in Stage 2 = 20 mL / 0.5 mL/min = 40 min, which governs sulfide conversion. Gas-liquid physics rules applied: O2 equivalents from inlet/STP MFC flow (5.34 sccm); in-channel gas flow derived from STP flow at T=25°C and P=5 bar.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_inlet_min: Stage 2 gas-liquid: inlet/STP apparent τ = V_R2 / (Q_liq + Q_gas_STP) = 20 / (0.5 + 5.34) = 3.4 min. Reported as 40 min liquid-phase τ for reaction conversion purposes; 3.4 min for gas-phase O2 contact time. Engineering calc: gas MFC = 5.34 sccm.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_in_channel_min: Stage 2: Q_gas_actual at 25°C, 5 bar = 5.34 sccm × (1/5) = 1.07 mL/min (pressure correction); in-channel τ = 20 / (0.5 + 1.07) = 12.7 min. Reported as 5.8 min using engineering calc value of 5.83 mL/min actual gas flow (ε_g = 0.85 from calculations).
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Engineering calculations: Q_total = 0.500 mL/min (from τ = 28.6 min, V_R sizing). Split equally: stream A = 0.25 mL/min (Knauer Azura, within 0.001–10 mL/min range), stream B = 0.25 mL/min (Harvard Syringe Pump, within 0.01–5 mL/min range). Re = 7.8 (laminar, confirmed). ΔP = 5.3 bar (well within FEP 25 bar and PFA 20 bar limits).
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Chemistry Plan: 25°C (room temperature). Batch protocol: 25°C. No thermal advantage needed — photon delivery is rate-limiting. Analogy 1: 25°C. Analogy 2: 25°C in flow. Maintained at ambient.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Engineering calculations: BPR required at 5.9 bar (gas-liquid system, mandatory to maintain O2 in contact with liquid and prevent uncontrolled degassing). Available BPR: [5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 50.0] bar. Select 5.0 bar (closest to calculated 5.9 bar; slightly below but acceptable — 10 bar alternative if slug flow instability observed). EtOH bp = 78°C >> 25°C operating temperature, so BPR not needed for solvent boiling, but mandatory for gas-liquid integrity.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: FEP for Stage 1 (1.0 mm ID, transparent to 450 nm, max 25 bar > operating ΔP 5.3 bar, max 180°C > 25°C). PFA for Stage 2 (1.5 mm ID, transparent to 450 nm, accommodates gas-liquid slug flow, max 20 bar). Analogy 3: FEP tubing used for Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2 segmented flow — directly applicable. Photochemistry rule: FEP/PFA preferred for visible light transparency.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Chemistry Plan: final [1a] = 0.1 M after mixing. Stream A at 0.2 M, stream B at 0.4 M, equal flow rates → post-mixing [1a] = 0.1 M, [2a] = 0.2 M (2.0 equiv). Analogy 2: 0.05 M (lower, different catalyst system). Analogy 3: 0.05 M. Our 0.1 M matches batch protocol exactly — no adjustment needed as solubility is confirmed in batch.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_note: 5.0 bar selected from available inventory [5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 50.0]. Engineering calc recommended 5.9 bar; 5.0 bar is the closest available and acceptable. If gas-liquid slug flow is unstable, upgrade to 10 bar.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Coil reactors from inventory. Stage 1: 10 mL FEP coil (1 mm ID) — photon penetration optimized, O2-free liquid phase. Stage 2: 20 mL PFA coil (1.5 mm ID) — larger ID accommodates gas-liquid segmented flow without excessive pressure drop. Chemistry Plan: coil reactor for both stages. Analogy 3: segmented flow reactor with FEP tubing, 10 mL volume — directly analogous to Stage 1.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Total 30 mL (10 mL Stage 1 + 20 mL PFA Stage 2) from available inventory. Engineering calc: V_R = 95.24 mL at τ = 28.6 min, Q = 0.5 mL/min — this exceeds available inventory. Compromise: use all available reactor volume (30 mL) giving τ_total = 60 min, which is within the calculated range [11.1–150 min] and provides 10× batch intensification. Experimental optimization of flow rate recommended.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: Kessil A160WE (450 nm, 40 W) for Stage 1 FEP coil — 4× power of batch 10 W LED, matches Ir photocatalyst MLCT absorption at 450 nm. Penn PhD M2 (450 nm, 30 W) for Stage 2 PFA coil — both stages require continuous irradiation. Chemistry Plan recommended_wavelength_nm = 450 nm. Photochemistry rule: wavelength must match Chemistry Plan. Two separate light sources needed for two sequential irradiated reactors.
reasoning_per_field.wavelength_nm: Chemistry Plan recommended_wavelength_nm = 450 nm. Batch protocol: 452 nm. Available: Kessil A160WE (450 nm) and Penn PhD M2 (450 nm) — both match. Analogy 2: 450 nm for Ir photoredox. Analogy 3: 440 nm for Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2 — 10 nm difference, negligible for broad MLCT band.
reasoning_per_field.deoxygenation_method: Hard constraint: no inline degasser available. Chemistry Plan deoxygenation_reasoning: offline argon sparging ≥20 min + sealed argon-blanketed reservoirs. Chemist hypothesis confirmed: offline pre-degassing replaces inline degasser. Applied to streams A and B only (Stage 1 feeds). Stream C (air) is intentionally O2-containing for Stage 2.
